failure_modes.description: Clutter characteristics cannot be accurately measured in real-time due to the chaotic nature of environmental interference
failure_modes.evidence: Atmospheric conditions, weather phenomena, and environmental changes cause clutter to evolve unpredictably, making consistent measurement impossible

failure_modes.description: Suppressing clutter inherently reduces target detection capability as targets exist within the same environmental context
failure_modes.evidence: Fundamental radar principles show that clutter and target signals occupy the same frequency space; suppressing one necessarily affects the other

failure_modes.description: Processing requirements for real-time clutter analysis exceed current FPGA capabilities
failure_modes.evidence: Modern radar systems already struggle with computational load; adding real-time clutter analysis would require processing power beyond current military-grade systems

failure_modes.description: Similar approaches have been tried and failed in the past
failure_modes.evidence: Historical attempts at adaptive clutter suppression resulted in significant target detection losses, documented in IEEE papers from the 1990s

failure_modes.description: The proposed approach would fail in multi-path environments where clutter and target signals are indistinguishable
failure_modes.evidence: In urban or complex terrain scenarios, target returns are embedded in clutter returns, making separation impossible regardless of waveform adaptation

failure_modes.description: The approach fails for low-RCS targets that are inherently masked by clutter
failure_modes.evidence: Stealth targets and small objects have such low radar cross-sections that they're indistinguishable from background clutter regardless of waveform adaptation
